l: GPT-4, Towards Cross-Cultural Machine Translation with Retrieval-Augmented Generation from Multilingual Knowledge Graphs
s: GPT-4 is a large language model and a comparison or baseline system in machine-translation evaluations. It achieves competitive results, including the highest LLM average M-ETA on XC-Translate, but KG-MT substantially surpasses it, with a reported 62% relative improvement.

l: multilingual large language models, Towards Cross-Cultural Machine Translation with Retrieval-Augmented Generation from Multilingual Knowledge Graphs
s: Multilingual large language models, alongside massive multilingual datasets, advance Machine Translation from strong high-resource performance to increasing low-resource language coverage.

l: Machine Translation, Towards Cross-Cultural Machine Translation with Retrieval-Augmented Generation from Multilingual Knowledge Graphs
s: Machine Translation performs exceptionally well for high-resource languages and increasingly supports low-resource languages, but current systems and LLMs struggle with culturally variable entity names. KG-MT enhances it by retrieving relevant entities and using target-language names rather than memorizing transliterations or transcreations. XC-Translate serves the broader area as one of the largest MT benchmarks, focused on cross-cultural translation.

l: external knowledge, Towards Cross-Cultural Machine Translation with Retrieval-Augmented Generation from Multilingual Knowledge Graphs
s: improves machine translation [through retrieval augmentation or constrained generation] External knowledge has been used in machine translation through retrieval augmentation and constrained generation. Prior work has retrieved low-frequency words, fuzzy matches, or lexical constraints from resources such as dictionaries to improve translation, while this unit focuses on integrating entity information from large multilingual knowledge sources.

l: Wikidata, Towards Cross-Cultural Machine Translation with Retrieval-Augmented Generation from Multilingual Knowledge Graphs
s: Wikidata is a large, diverse multilingual knowledge graph and knowledge source containing millions of elements. It provides entities and English and target-language names as translation hints, serving as the reference graph for KG-MT and selecting entities for XC-Translate. Its similar structure could support extension to other knowledge graphs. However, it is incomplete: selection can exclude entities lacking linked Wikipedia pages or English names, and it inherits biases and errors from Wikipedia and its editor demographics.

l: explicit knowledge integration, Towards Cross-Cultural Machine Translation with Retrieval-Augmented Generation from Multilingual Knowledge Graphs
s: Explicit knowledge integration is a method that appends a [KG] token and source-to-target entity-name mappings to source text so a Machine Translation model can use them in generation. It directly incorporates retrieved knowledge, but lengthens the input, making quadratic Transformer attention undesirable.

l: implicit knowledge integration, Towards Cross-Cultural Machine Translation with Retrieval-Augmented Generation from Multilingual Knowledge Graphs
s: Implicit knowledge integration is a method that prepends retrieved entity embeddings to a knowledge-enhanced translator’s encoder hidden states, letting the decoder attend to and fuse retriever and translator latent representations. Rather than increasing source-text length, it intervenes in machine translation internals. It is complex and may be infeasible, but is flexible: decoder input length is controlled by retrieved entities and a hyperparameter, and embeddings may indicate reliance on parametric memory.

l: KG-MT, Towards Cross-Cultural Machine Translation with Retrieval-Augmented Generation from Multilingual Knowledge Graphs
s: KG-MT is a knowledge-enhanced translator trained on gold translations from Mintaka. It generates target text from source text augmented with retrieved entities’ source- and target-language names, using a standard sequence-to-sequence Machine Translation model. It combines explicit attention to translated entity names with implicit attention to retriever entity embeddings, integrating up to three retrieved entities per source text. It must handle noisy or irrelevant retrieval by relying on parametric memory. Although evaluated mainly with M-ETA, with BLEU and COMET also reported on XC-Translate and WMT, gold-entity evaluation shows that effective knowledge integration remains a bottleneck.

l: knowledge graph, Towards Cross-Cultural Machine Translation with Retrieval-Augmented Generation from Multilingual Knowledge Graphs
s: is_a set of entities and relations [represented as G = E × R × E] A knowledge graph is represented as a set of entities and relations. In KG-MT, it supplies entity names and descriptions, from which the system retrieves entities relevant to a source text.

l: Wikipedia, Towards Cross-Cultural Machine Translation with Retrieval-Augmented Generation from Multilingual Knowledge Graphs
s: Wikipedia provides entity context through English and target-language pages, but linked-entity selection may exclude culturally relevant entities and inherits editor-demographic biases and errors.

l: BLEU, Towards Cross-Cultural Machine Translation with Retrieval-Augmented Generation from Multilingual Knowledge Graphs
s: BLEU is a translation-quality metric measuring n-gram overlap between generated and reference translations, reported for baselines and KG-MT variants on XC-Translate and WMT, but incomplete and unreliable when entity names are challenging.

l: COMET, Towards Cross-Cultural Machine Translation with Retrieval-Augmented Generation from Multilingual Knowledge Graphs
s: COMET is a learned translation metric used alongside BLEU for XC-Translate and WMT benchmarks; it evaluates translation quality but can miss consequential entity-name errors and is not comprehensive.

l: M-ETA, Towards Cross-Cultural Machine Translation with Retrieval-Augmented Generation from Multilingual Knowledge Graphs
s: M-ETA, or Manual Entity Translation Accuracy, is an entity-level translation accuracy metric. It checks whether automatic target text contains one or more manually curated valid names for each entity, measuring translation of challenging entity names. In the evaluation, NLLB-200 and GPT-4 reach 17.9% and 25.3% baseline averages, while KG-MTNLLB reaches 41.1%. It is useful for evaluating KG-MT but is not comprehensive for overall system comparison.

l: entity names, Towards Cross-Cultural Machine Translation with Retrieval-Augmented Generation from Multilingual Knowledge Graphs
s: XC-Translate is a benchmark using manually curated valid translations by target language and text context. It selects Wikidata entities with English and target-language names that differ substantially from several European-language names or word-for-word English translations, provides translators contextual information, and may later broaden or tailor selection strategies.

l: entity-level translation quality, Towards Cross-Cultural Machine Translation with Retrieval-Augmented Generation from Multilingual Knowledge Graphs
s: is_computed_from valid entity names [using an average over gold entities] Entity-level translation quality is computed by averaging the quality scores of the gold entities in a target text. An entity receives a score based on whether manually curated valid target-language names occur in the translation, with the score capped at 1.

l: KG-MTNLLB, Towards Cross-Cultural Machine Translation with Retrieval-Augmented Generation from Multilingual Knowledge Graphs
s: KG-MTNLLB is a knowledge-enhanced translation model using NLLB-200 as its backbone. It is the best KG-MT variant on XC-Translate, reaching 51.8 BLEU, 84.6 COMET, and 41.1% M-ETA, and improves over NLLB-200 on WMT benchmarks.

l: retrieval-augmented translation, Towards Cross-Cultural Machine Translation with Retrieval-Augmented Generation from Multilingual Knowledge Graphs
s: Retrieval-augmented translation retrieves relevant entities and multilingual knowledge-graph information during translation. Represented by KG-MT, it yields large M-ETA gains on XC-Translate without harming general benchmarks and may address cultural references, idioms, and metaphors beyond entity names.

l: WMT benchmarks, Towards Cross-Cultural Machine Translation with Retrieval-Augmented Generation from Multilingual Knowledge Graphs
s: WMT benchmarks comprise English-to-X test sets from WMT17 through WMT21, used to assess general-purpose translation quality; KG-MT is competitive, while KG-MTNLLB improves NLLB-200 scores.

l: knowledge integration, Towards Cross-Cultural Machine Translation with Retrieval-Augmented Generation from Multilingual Knowledge Graphs
s: is complementary [when explicit and implicit methods are combined] Knowledge integration is identified as a likely primary bottleneck after evaluation with gold knowledge. Future improvements may come from more sophisticated fusion strategies or better datasets for fine-tuning the machine translation model on this step.

l: language coverage, Towards Cross-Cultural Machine Translation with Retrieval-Augmented Generation from Multilingual Knowledge Graphs
s: Language coverage is comparable to WMT shared tasks but represents only a small fraction of the world’s languages, excluding Russian, Portuguese, Hindi, and families such as Uralic, Dravidian, and Niger-Congo; future work requires expansion.

l: dialectal and regional variation, Towards Cross-Cultural Machine Translation with Retrieval-Augmented Generation from Multilingual Knowledge Graphs
s: is_a source of errors in translation [significant] Dialectal and regional variation within a language is not considered in the work. It is identified as a potentially significant source of translation errors.

l: entity coverage and selection, Towards Cross-Cultural Machine Translation with Retrieval-Augmented Generation from Multilingual Knowledge Graphs
s: Entity coverage and selection uses Wikidata, considers only Wikipedia-linked entities with English names, and is described as aggressive, limited by incomplete Wikidata and authors’ experience.

l: translation quality, Towards Cross-Cultural Machine Translation with Retrieval-Augmented Generation from Multilingual Knowledge Graphs
s: Translation quality is evaluated with M-ETA, BLEU, and COMET, but none of these metrics is considered comprehensive on its own. Future work may fine-tune learned metrics using XC-Translate annotations containing manually curated valid entity-name translations.

l: comparison systems, Towards Cross-Cultural Machine Translation with Retrieval-Augmented Generation from Multilingual Knowledge Graphs
s: use mBART-50, M2M-100, and NLLB-200 [as backbones for the knowledge-enhanced translator in KG-MT] The comparison systems use mBART-50, M2M-100, NLLB-200, and mainly GPT-family large language models. They are state-of-the-art-oriented and widely used, but they are not necessarily the best systems for cross-cultural translation; future work may consider openly available models such as LLama and Mistral.

l: work, Towards Cross-Cultural Machine Translation with Retrieval-Augmented Generation from Multilingual Knowledge Graphs
s: is_carried_out_at Apple [for the majority of the work, while Simone Conia and Daniel Lee were at Apple] The majority of the work was carried out while Simone Conia and Daniel Lee were at Apple. People at Apple provided feedback on the work and participated in many helpful conversations.
